1991-01.title: Sandra Lovelace v. Northeast Presbytery
1991-01.summary: Sandra Lovelace submitted two letters challenging actions of Northeast Presbytery; the SJC found both administratively and judicially out of order because the first had not been presented first to the lower court and the second lacked supporting reasons and identified no complainable presbytery action under BCO 43-2 and 43-3.
1991-01.disposition_detail: Both letters found administratively and judicially out of order

1991-03.title: Daniel R. Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
1991-03.summary: Grace Presbyterian Church challenged Covenant Presbytery's handling of protests and complaints concerning its refusal to institute process against Daniel R. Morse and Curtis I. Crenshaw. The SJC directed that the two ministers be removed from the presbytery roll under BCO 38-3, held that Grace could withdraw under BCO 25-11 without prior notice, and recorded that Grace's complaints had been abandoned as moot.
1991-03.disposition_detail: Complaints abandoned as moot; SJC issued final directions on ministerial and congregational roll status

1991-04.title: Robert D. Hopper v. James River Presbytery
1991-04.summary: TE Robert Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's restriction on teaching and preaching about present-day prophecy and tongues. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that presbytery may limit such teaching for the welfare of the church when it determines the views threaten the church's peace or purity, while declining to issue a comprehensive doctrinal ruling.

1991-05.title: Herman Gunter III et al. v. Central Florida Presbytery
1991-05.summary: Herman Gunter III and Donald Monroe challenged their Session's refusal to approve them for examination as ruling elders based on its assessment of their theonomic views and alleged divisiveness. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session could evaluate theological and character issues affecting eligibility for office and could exercise judgment for the church's peace and purity.
1991-05.standard_of_review_detail: The Session's eligibility judgment was to be sustained absent capricious action or bad faith.

1991-07.title: Complainants v. Potomac Presbytery
1991-07.summary: Complainants challenged Potomac Presbytery's handling of a dispute over the dissolution of pastoral relationships at Timonium Presbyterian Church. The SJC did not sustain the timely complaint, dismissed two related complaints as untimely under BCO 43-2, and deferred to the lower court's judgment absent demonstrated constitutional error.
1991-07.disposition_detail: Timely complaint not sustained; two related complaints dismissed as untimely
1991-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC would not overturn a competent lower court absent a clear constitutional violation or other demonstrated error.

1992-05.title: Parks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
1992-05.summary: Parks and others challenged Northside Session's plan for multiple elder resignations, pastor severance, a delayed pastoral call, and bylaw revisions. The SJC denied every specification, holding that the plan did not violate BCO 24-6, 20-6, 20-2, or 25-7; a dissent was recorded.

1992-07.title: Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery (Case #2)
1992-07.summary: Conrad and others challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's refusal to institute process against TE Stephen Stout and to permit them to act as voluntary prosecutors. The SJC denied both claims, holding that the presbytery properly found no strong presumption of guilt and retained authority over voluntary prosecution under BCO 31-1 through 31-3.

2000-07.title: Ed Stadick v. Northern Illinois Presbytery
2000-07.summary: RE Ed Stadick filed a complaint against Northern Illinois Presbytery, but the SJC found the case out of order because it was not filed within the applicable time limit.
2000-07.disposition_detail: Found out of order because not timely filed

2002-17.title: Sung K. Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery
2002-17.summary: TE Sung K. Kim appealed his deposition by Korean Capital Presbytery, but the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial as required by BCO 42-2; the underlying contumacy finding and deposition were therefore not reviewed on the merits.
2002-17.disposition_detail: Appeal found judicially out of order under BCO 42-2

2002-18.title: Mark Herzor and Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery
2002-18.summary: TEs Mark Herzor and Erwin Morrison challenged a Philadelphia Presbytery matter arising from a judicial commission's actions. The SJC found the complaint judicially out of order because it targeted the commission rather than completed presbytery action under BCO 15-3 and 43-1.
2002-18.disposition_detail: Complaint found judicially out of order under BCO 15-3 and 43-1

2003-07.title: Aureliano Tan v. South Texas Presbytery
2003-07.summary: TE Aureliano Tan complained against South Texas Presbytery, but the SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because the presbytery had not yet heard it; the matter was premature and received no merits review.
2003-07.disposition_detail: Complaint found administratively out of order because prematurely filed

2004-06.title: Aureliano Tan Jr. v. Houston Metro Presbytery
2004-06.summary: TE Aureliano Tan Jr. appealed Houston Metro Presbytery's action, but the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial as required by BCO 42-2.
2004-06.disposition_detail: Appeal found judicially out of order under BCO 42-2

2008-10.title: Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
2008-10.summary: RE Mark Grasso and others challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensure and ordination of Jason Hsu, who held a stated difference concerning women deacons but affirmed willingness to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed the presbytery's actions, holding that the stated difference did not bar licensure or ordination; a dissent was recorded.

2009-01.title: Morton H. Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery
2009-01.summary: TE Morton H. Smith challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's ruling that his complaint was filed too late. The SJC disposed of the matter by reference to its decision in Case 2008-15, without a separate merits analysis in the 2009-01 section.
2009-01.disposition_detail: Answered by reference to the SJC decision in Case 2008-15

2011-16.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (duplicate of Case 2011-15)
2011-16.summary: Case 2011-16 duplicated Case 2011-15 in Steven Hahn's consolidated complaints against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's refusal to institute process against Lisa Ridenour, RE Glen Ridenour, and TE Eric Huber. The SJC denied the complaint, deferring to the presbytery's judgment under BCO 31-8 absent clear error.

2016-10.title: Korean Northwest Presbytery
2016-10.summary: The SJC reviewed Korean Northwest Presbytery's amended and corrected response to exceptions in the review of its records and accepted the response by roll-call vote, with one dissent and one abstention recorded.

2018-01.title: Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
2018-01.summary: RE Glen Mapes appealed his conviction and censures by a temporary session of New Hope Christian Church. The SJC sustained the appeal in part, affirming the finding that he failed to submit to church government but reversing the excessive suspension and deposition and replacing them with admonition; the related complaint was moot after the church left the PCA.
2018-01.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part; censures reversed and replaced with admonition; related complaint moot

2021-08.title: Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
2021-08.summary: The SJC cited Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery to respond to an exception in the review of its records. When no adopted response had arrived by the March 3, 2022 meeting, the SJC allowed time for the presbytery to adopt and file one and warned that failure could lead to a further appearance; no merits disposition appears in this record.
2021-08.disposition_detail: Citation and response process; no merits disposition in this record

2022-17.title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
2022-17.summary: Peter Benyola's three complaints against Central Florida Presbytery were found administratively out of order because he was no longer a member of a PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing; the SJC did not reach the merits.
2022-17.disposition_detail: Complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing

2013-05.title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
2013-05.summary: Steven Hahn asked the SJC to assume original jurisdiction over Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery. The SJC catalog records the matter as administratively out of order, and no merits opinion has been located in the local corpus.
2013-05.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; request to assume original jurisdiction not heard

2023-06.title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
2023-06.summary: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main—finding the Blue Hen complaint moot and improperly taken up, the document directive partly overbroad, and the stay improper—while rejecting one complaint and not reaching impartiality; concurring opinions were recorded.
2023-06.disposition_detail: Complaints sustained in the main; one specification denied and one not reached

2023-15.title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
2023-15.summary: RE Tom Turner challenged South Florida Presbytery's handling of matters involving Cross Community Church and the discipline of its pastor after the church voted to disaffiliate from the PCA. The SJC ruled the complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing because the church had already disaffiliated, a conclusion opposed by two dissenting commissioners.
2023-15.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing

2025-12.title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
2025-12.summary: TEs Felipe Assis and Carter Brown appealed South Florida Presbytery's decision to divest them without censure after their churches left the PCA and they remained without transferred credentials. The SJC sustained the appeal, holding that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 did not authorize the divestiture on these facts, returned the ministers to good standing, and directed Presbytery to dissolve the existing calls and pursue a constitutionally appropriate course; two specifications could not be judged on the record.
2025-12.disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestiture reversed and ministers returned to good standing

1977-01.summary: Rev. Paul Karlberg and RE James Luce challenged Central Georgia Presbytery's handling of conflict at Faith Presbyterian Church, alleging that its commission had been biased and improperly constituted as a judicial commission. The Assembly's judicial commission did not sustain the complaint after the presbytery changed the body to a pastoral commission, rescinded most recommendations, and ended the investigation; it found no substantive reason to remand the matter.
1977-01.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; no substantive reason to remand after presbytery corrected and ended the commission's work

1978-01.summary: RE James Campbell challenged Mid-Atlantic Presbytery's approval of a commission report that rejected charges against Rev. Robert Schoof as inadmissible and limited the investigation. The Assembly directed the presbytery to hold a new hearing on the original charges under BCO 44-5, conform to the BCO, and keep the principals informed; it also appointed a judicial commission for any further appeal before the next Assembly.
1978-01.disposition_detail: New hearing ordered under BCO 44-5; judicial commission appointed for a potential further appeal

1980-03.summary: TEs Byron Snapp and James Hope challenged Calvary Presbytery's use of the extraordinary clause to examine a candidate for ordination who had taken only one quarter of Hebrew and had no demonstrated extraordinary circumstance or gift. The Assembly sustained the error, held that the presbytery had not justified the exception, and remanded the matter for correction while directing preparation of guidance on the proper use of the extraordinary clause.
1980-03.disposition_detail: Error sustained; ordination matter remanded to Calvary Presbytery for correction

1981-01.summary: RE Cooke Lewis and others challenged Grace Presbytery's administration of Ellisville Presbyterian Church, including the composition and appointment of an administrative commission and the refusal to dissolve the pastoral relationship after a congregational vote. The Assembly's judicial commission found no BCO violation and did not sustain any item or the complaint as a whole, while urging the parties to continue reconciliation.
1981-01.disposition_detail: Items 1–3 and the complaint as a whole not sustained; no BCO violation found
1981-01.standard_of_review_detail: The complaint expressly challenged presbytery judgment and discretion; no constitutional violation was found.

1982-04.summary: TE Vaughn Hathaway and others challenged Grace Presbytery's refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against TE G. Aiken Taylor. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas Presbytery had not refused jurisdiction, but directed it to proceed under BCO 32-3 and following and held that the BCO 32-20 limitation did not apply because its earlier commission had delayed formal process.
1982-04.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained conditionally; Western Carolinas Presbytery directed to proceed under BCO 32-3 and following

1982-05.summary: The Session of Peace Presbyterian Church challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery's resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcoholic beverages the proper Christian lifestyle and urging officers and Sessions to follow it. The Assembly sustained the complaint, holding that the resolution in its present form bound consciences beyond Scripture and the Westminster Confession; the presbytery was directed to rescind it.
1982-05.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; total-abstinence resolution held to bind conscience beyond Scripture
1982-05.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment interpreted the constitutional prohibition against binding conscience by human commands in WCF 20-2.

1983-01.summary: TE Robert Reymond and others challenged Illiana Presbytery's handling of a teaching elder's confessed adultery and related violations, arguing that the presbytery reduced the charges and imposed a censure not commensurate with the offenses. The Assembly sustained the complaint in all parts, held that BCO 34-7 procedures and a more proportionate judgment were required, and remanded the case to Illiana Presbytery for a new trial.
1983-01.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in all parts; case remanded for a new trial under proper BCO procedure
1983-01.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment reviewed the lower court's disciplinary procedure and proportionality against BCO 34-7.

1983-02.summary: RE Val Barleman and others challenged Ascension Presbytery's approval of Kurt Lutjens's ordination trials despite exceptions concerning admission to the Lord's Supper, baptism, Sabbath observance, baptism by immersion, and women serving as deacons. The Assembly sustained the complaint and annulled the presbytery's action sustaining the trials, while directing correction of the nonconforming portions and pastoral counsel; it did not itself annul the ordination or remove Lutjens from the presbytery roll, and a protest was recorded.
1983-02.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; ordination-trial action annulled, with corrective and pastoral directions; protest recorded
1983-02.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment determined whether stated exceptions conformed to the PCA's constitutional standards.

1983-07.summary: TE Stark Wilbor and others challenged North Georgia Presbytery's approval of John Parrish's examination for transfer of license even though he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The Assembly sustained the error, annulled the presbytery's action, and directed instruction and re-examination on the doctrine; a dissent was recorded.
1983-07.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; action sustaining the transfer-license examination annulled; instruction and re-examination directed
1983-07.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment interpreted the Sabbath doctrine required by the Westminster Confession and Catechisms.

1983-08.summary: TE Jack Eubanks and RE Milton Shelby challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's called meeting and its dissolution and reconstitution of a judicial commission during the New Life Presbyterian Church conflict. The Assembly sustained the objections to dissolving the commission without a two-thirds vote and to the commission's subsequent action, but did not sustain the challenges to the called meeting, presbytery authority over church membership, or David Alexander's complaint; the case concerns procedure rather than a merits ruling on membership.
1983-08.disposition_detail: Items 2 and 3 sustained; Items 1, 4, and 5 not sustained
1983-08.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment primarily resolved procedural and jurisdictional questions.

1983-09.summary: The Session of Village Chapel challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery's decision to lift a matter from the table, alleging improper evidence and an accelerated decision. The Assembly's commission deemed the complaint abandoned when the complainant failed to appear after proper notice, and confirmed advice declining to answer questions that belonged in complaint or review proceedings while referring the remaining question to BCO 25-2.
1983-09.disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned for nonappearance under BCO 42-10; interim advice on Reference 8 confirmed

1983-12.summary: TE Jack Eubanks and others challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's handling of the New Life conflict, focusing on the moderator's conflict of interest and voting privileges and on whether a higher court could determine the membership of a lower church. The Assembly sustained the first three items concerning the moderator and reserved judgment on the membership question because it had not yet ruled on that issue.
1983-12.disposition_detail: Items 1–3 sustained; judgment on Item 4 reserved

1983-13.summary: TE Donald Codling and others challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery's denial of Ron Harris's licensure after the presbytery changed its standing rules during the meeting to require a higher vote and declined to consider relevant evidence and preaching samples. The Assembly sustained the complaint in part—finding the rule change illegal and several stated reasons insufficient to deny licensure—and urged presbytery to re-examine Harris; other specifications were not sustained and a dissent was recorded.
1983-13.disposition_detail: Specifications 1, 4, 5, and 6 sustained; specifications 2 and 3 not sustained; re-examination urged
1983-13.standard_of_review_detail: The judgment evaluated the presbytery's examination and licensure judgment for procedural and evidentiary error.

1983-15.summary: TE W. Ted Smith complained that Central Carolina Presbytery failed to carry out Assembly and presbytery directives concerning restoration and oversight of members of New Life Presbyterian Church and asked for dissolution of the pastor's pastoral relationship and censure. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because it was not properly a complaint but appeared to be a protest, while noting that much of its substance had been addressed in related cases and directing a broader response to the New Life conflict.
1983-15.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained as improperly framed; matter treated as a protest, with substance addressed in related cases

1980-02.summary: TE Rod Mays brought an appeal against New River Presbytery alleging that it failed to address reported scandalous activity involving one of its ministers. The official case catalog preserves only that issue description and no final merits judgment, so this record remains a source-recovery item rather than a substantive holding.
1980-02.disposition_detail: Issue recorded in the official catalog; final merits disposition not located

1983-14.summary: RE Truman Swain and others brought a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery. The official SJC catalog records the matter as abandoned, with no merits judgment published in the available record.
1983-14.disposition_detail: Complaint abandoned; no merits judgment located

1998-03.summary: Williams appealed an action of South Texas Presbytery. The SJC approved the panel's dismissal because the appeal was administratively out of order, and therefore did not reach the merits.
1998-03.disposition_detail: Appeal dismissed as administratively out of order

1998-07.summary: Yi challenged Korean Capital Presbytery after the presbytery acted in a called meeting, but did not file the required complaint against that completed action. The SJC found the matter administratively out of order and did not review the merits.
1998-07.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order because no complaint was filed after lower-court action

2000-03.summary: South Coast Presbytery's memorial was withdrawn before the SJC issued a merits decision. The record therefore preserves no substantive holding.

2000-05.summary: Robert H. King filed a complaint against Evangel Presbytery, but abandoned it before adjudication. The matter appears only as a docket entry and has no merits holding.

2001-35.summary: Moon K. Ham and others presented allegations to Korean Capital Presbytery but did not frame them as a complaint against a presbytery action or inaction. The record identifies BCO 43-1 as the controlling procedural point and contains no merits ruling.
2001-35.disposition_detail: Allegations not presented in the form of a complaint against presbytery action under BCO 43-1

2001-36.summary: Moo S. Lim and others' complaint against Korean Capital Presbytery became moot after related Cases 2000-09 and 2001-08 were decided. The SJC issued no independent opinion or merits findings.
2001-36.disposition_detail: Moot in light of related cases; no independent opinion or findings

2007-06.summary: TE Eliot Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery's handling of his stated-supply relationship, including whether the interim-pastor relationship was prematurely dissolved and whether the terms had been properly distinguished. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed presbytery's decision; it also held that the related actions of the presbytery's commissions were properly taken.
2007-06.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; Korean Eastern Presbytery's decision affirmed
2007-06.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed presbytery judgment concerning the pastoral relationship with deference.

2007-07.summary: RE Sae H. Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery's appointment of a commission to approve a stated supply. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed that BCO 15-2 authorized the presbytery to appoint a commission for this type of ministerial relationship.
2007-07.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; appointment and scope of stated-supply commission affirmed under BCO 15-2
2007-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted BCO 15-2's authority to appoint commissions.

2008-01.summary: The Session of Crossroads Community Church challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination of a candidate who stated a difference concerning women and the office of deacon but agreed to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed presbytery's judgment, holding that the candidate's stated willingness to comply with the BCO and affirm the ordination vow supported the decision; a dissent argued the complaint should have been sustained.
2008-01.disposition_detail: Complaints denied; Philadelphia Presbytery's licensing and ordination decisions affirmed; dissent recorded
2008-01.standard_of_review_detail: Constitutional interpretation was combined with deferential review of presbytery judgment under BCO 39-3.

2011-11.summary: Steven Hahn challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's handling of complaints arising from Christ the King's restriction on his attendance while he sought a psychiatric evaluation. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session's action was pastoral guidance rather than judicial censure and that no clear error was shown in the lower courts' judgment.
2011-11.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; pastoral restriction and lower-court judgment affirmed
2011-11.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC applied deferential review to the lower court's judgment and found no clear error.

2011-12.summary: Steven Hahn appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension from the sacraments by Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery after a disciplinary trial arising from his disputes with Christ the King Session and related individuals. The SJC denied the appeal, finding that the record did not establish clear error in the trial or judgment despite contrary evidence.
2011-12.disposition_detail: Appeal denied; disciplinary judgment affirmed because no clear error was shown
2011-12.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC stated that it would not reverse a lower-court judgment absent clear error.

2011-15.summary: Steven Hahn challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's refusal to institute process against Lisa and Glen Ridenour and TE Eric Huber. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that decisions whether to commence process are matters of court discretion and judgment subject to review for clear error, which the record did not establish; a concurring opinion explained the distinction between alleging an offense and requiring formal charges.
2011-15.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; refusal to institute process affirmed; concurring opinion recorded
2011-15.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC treated institution of process as a matter of discretion and judgment reviewable for clear error under BCO 39-3.

1997-09.summary: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.
1997-09.disposition_detail: Excommunication reversed; remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5
1997-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC described deferential review of lower-court factual and discretionary judgments and found the highest censure unsupported by the record.

2000-09.summary: TE Sung Keon Kim challenged Korean Capital Presbytery's suspension of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington Session and replacement of its functions by a presbytery commission without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, held that the presbytery lacked authority to take that action under the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six, and annulled the commission's subsequent acts.
2000-09.disposition_detail: Presbytery action and subsequent commission acts annulled for unauthorized replacement of the Session
2000-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six to define presbytery authority over a local Session.

2001-01.summary: RE Charles Kim appealed discipline imposed by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission that had replaced the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to the Session, not the presbytery commission, reversed the presbytery's action and censure, and held that the commission's acts were unauthorized without congregational consent.
2001-01.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed; original jurisdiction belonged to the local Session
2001-01.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted constitutional jurisdiction over communicant members and the authority of the local Session.

2001-03.summary: TE Sung Keon Kim appealed a five-year suspension imposed after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission judged him guilty by a process that did not properly serve an indictment or preserve an adequate trial record. The SJC sustained the procedural challenge, found noncompliance with BCO 32 and 34, and remanded for a new trial conducted under those chapters.
2001-03.disposition_detail: Procedural error sustained; remanded for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34
2001-03.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed the trial record for procedural error and found the process constitutionally inadequate.

2001-04.summary: RE Moon K. Ham appealed a three-year suspension imposed by Korean Capital Presbytery's commission after it assumed original jurisdiction over charges against him. The SJC held that the local Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction for a communicant member, reversed the presbytery and commission actions, and rejected the resulting censure.
2001-04.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed; original jurisdiction belonged to the local Session
2001-04.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over communicant members.

2001-07.summary: TE Andy Lee challenged Korean Capital Presbytery's suspension of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington Session and appointment of a commission to act for it without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained both issues, holding the presbytery lacked authority for the intervention and annulling all subsequent acts of the commission acting as Session.
2001-07.disposition_detail: Both specifications sustained; intervention and subsequent commission acts annulled
2001-07.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted BCO 13-9 in relation to the BCO's protections for local church governance.

2001-09.summary: RE Charles Kim appealed discipline imposed by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission appointed to hear charges against him. The SJC held that the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington was the proper court of original jurisdiction for a communicant member, reversed the presbytery and commission actions, and set aside the censure.
2001-09.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-09.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted which court constitutionally held original jurisdiction over the member.

2001-10.summary: RE Charles Kim appealed his excommunication by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission appointed to adjudicate charges against him. The SJC held that the local Session, not the presbytery commission, had original jurisdiction over the communicant member, reversed the lower-court action, and set aside the excommunication.
2001-10.disposition_detail: Excommunication and related lower-court action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-10.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over communicant members.

2001-12.summary: Deacon Peter Lee appealed discipline imposed by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission appointed to adjudicate charges against him. The SJC held that the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington was the proper court of original jurisdiction, reversed the presbytery and commission actions, and set aside the censure.
2001-12.disposition_detail: Presbytery and commission action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-12.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over a communicant member.

2001-14.summary: RE Moon K. Ham appealed his excommunication by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission appointed to adjudicate charges against him. The SJC held that the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington was the proper court of original jurisdiction, reversed the presbytery and commission actions, and set aside the excommunication.
2001-14.disposition_detail: Excommunication and related lower-court action reversed for lack of original jurisdiction
2001-14.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted the constitutional allocation of original jurisdiction over the member.

2001-19.summary: TE Sung Keon Kim appealed his deposition after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission conducted judicial process without serving an indictment and without an adequate record of the proceeding. The SJC sustained the procedural challenge, held that BCO 32 and 34 had not been followed, and remanded for a new trial under those chapters.
2001-19.disposition_detail: Procedural error sustained; deposition matter remanded for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34
2001-19.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC reviewed the lower-court record for procedural error and found it constitutionally inadequate.

1989-11.summary: The Session of Grace Presbyterian Church challenged Covenant Presbytery's refusal to examine a ruling elder again when he sought installation as an associate pastor. The adjudicating commission did not sustain the complaint, concluding that the BCO was ambiguous and PCA practice lacked sufficient consensus to require the additional ordination step.
1989-11.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained; BCO ambiguity and lack of PCA consensus supported presbytery's position

1997-16.summary: The Session of BPC Concord complained against Central Carolina Presbytery. The SJC did not sustain the complaint by an 11–7 vote, and two dissenting opinions were recorded; the available case record does not preserve a fuller statement of the underlying issue.
1997-16.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained 11–7; two dissents recorded; underlying issue not fully preserved in available record

2002-13.summary: RE David Lachman challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's appointment of a commission to hear a memorial and its adoption of the commission's report, alleging a grossly unconstitutional proceeding. The SJC found no such constitutional error and upheld the presbytery's handling of the memorial under BCO 40-5, while recording the matter as out of order rather than issuing a broader merits judgment.
2002-13.disposition_detail: Out of order; no unconstitutional proceeding found and BCO 40-5 memorial procedure upheld

2007-04.summary: TE Stephen Engel challenged Evangel Presbytery's handling of his appeal from Redeemer Session's direct suspension of him from the Lord's Supper while it accused him of contentiousness and rebellion. The SJC held that the Session had not conducted a trial, but that presbytery erred by failing to remand the matter under BCO 42-9 for proper process or dismissal; the complaint was sustained and sent back for rehearing.
2007-04.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained in part on remand duty; matter returned for proper process or dismissal under BCO 42-9
2007-04.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC deferred on the absence of a trial record but found constitutional error in the failure to remand.

2007-13.summary: TE David Kniseley and others challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's approval of the public title “Minister of Church Life” for an unordained female staff member. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that “minister” has a specific technical meaning in the BCO but that the BCO is silent on generic titles for non-ordained staff, leaving that use to lower-court judgment subject to BCO 40-2(3); a dissent disagreed.
2007-13.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; BCO meaning and generic use of title distinguished; dissent recorded
2007-13.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC interpreted BCO terminology and reserved generic-title propriety to lower-court judgment under BCO 40-2(3).

2008-16.summary: TEs Jeff Hutchinson and Craig Bulkeley challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's handling of RE Neill Payne's confession after a BCO 31-2 investigation, including the decision to use a case without process and impose indefinite suspension from office. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the request to find additional unconfessed sins would improperly bypass the procedures for instituting process and that the presbytery acted within its discretion.
2008-16.disposition_detail: Complaint denied; presbytery's handling of confession and indefinite suspension affirmed
2008-16.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC treated the presbytery's disciplinary judgment as discretionary and did not find clear error.

2009-05.summary: TE Martin Payne and related complainants challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations concerning TE Craig Bulkeley and its conclusion that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.
2009-05.disposition_detail: Specifications not sustained; BCO 31-2 investigation and no-strong-presumption finding affirmed
2009-05.standard_of_review_detail: The SJC expressly applied great deference to the lower court's investigative discretion under BCO 39-3(3).

2009-06.summary: TE James Bordwine and others challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's handling of study reports on TE Peter Leithart's Federal Vision-related teachings and its refusal to declare those views either orthodox or out of accord with the Standards without judicial process. The SJC sustained the complaint, held that presbytery erred in declaring the views not out of accord, and remanded for pastoral counsel or BCO 31-2 action; concurring and dissenting opinions were recorded.
2009-06.disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; presbytery's declaration reversed and matter remanded for counsel or BCO 31-2 action
2009-06.standard_of_review_detail: The case combined constitutional interpretation of doctrinal conformity with deferential review of investigative procedure.

2010-14.summary: Art Sartorius and others challenged Siouxlands Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of reports concerning TE Joshua Moon and its failure to find a strong presumption of guilt. The SJC did not sustain the complaint by a 19–1 vote; the official record preserves concurring and dissenting opinions but no broader merits ruling on the underlying reports.
2010-14.disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained 19–1; concurring and dissenting opinions recorded
2010-14.standard_of_review_detail: The issue concerned factual and discretionary investigative judgments under BCO 31-2 and 39-3.

2006-04.summary: TE David Peffley’s matter against Heritage Presbytery was found out of order and was not heard on the merits. The official record therefore provides no SJC judgment on the underlying dispute.
2006-04.disposition_detail: Out of order; matter not heard on the merits
2006-04.standard_of_review_detail: The matter ended procedurally before a merits standard of review was required.

2010-02.summary: TE Cutler’s matter against Platte Valley Presbytery was ruled administratively out of order. It was not heard on the merits, and no substantive SJC decision is recorded in the official case listing.
2010-02.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; no merits decision
2010-02.standard_of_review_detail: The matter ended procedurally before a merits standard of review was required.

2010-25.summary: TE Yuan’s matter against South Coast Presbytery was ruled administratively out of order. The official listing records no decision on the merits or substantive judicial reasoning.
2010-25.disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; no merits decision
2010-25.standard_of_review_detail: The matter ended procedurally before a merits standard of review was required.

2017-13.summary: TE David Tripp’s appeal against Ohio Valley Presbytery was withdrawn before the SJC issued a decision. No opinion text or merits disposition is recorded in the official case listing.
2017-13.disposition_detail: Withdrawn before decision; no merits disposition
2017-13.standard_of_review_detail: The matter ended before the SJC reached the merits.

2022-14.summary: TE Sung Bok Oh withdrew his complaint against Korean Southeast Presbytery on August 29, 2022. The SJC therefore recorded a procedural disposition without reaching the merits of the complaint.
2022-14.disposition_detail: Complaint withdrawn; dismissed without merits decision
2022-14.standard_of_review_detail: The complaint ended by withdrawal before merits review was required.
